basics.name: Obed Junias
basics.label: Computer Science Graduate Student & NLP Researcher
basics.summary: I am a graduate researcher at the BLAST Lab exploring natural language reasoning, LLM safety, and agentic systems. My primary research investigates the fundamental reliability of generative models, focusing on data quality and model collapse during foundation model pretraining. Following my work on interpretable commonsense reasoning (ACL 2026), my overarching vision is to pioneer advancements that ensure next-generation AI systems remain capable, transparent, logically grounded, and aligned with human outcomes.

research.organization: Institute of Cognitive Science, CU Boulder
research.summary: Conducting fairness and bias evaluations of large language models (LLaMA, GPT-4, etc.) in mental health classification tasks, analyzing demographic and modality-based disparities in model behavior.
highlights: Implemented fairness-aware loss functions and diagnostic probes for LLM evaluation
Identified demographic and linguistic biases in model outputs across text and audio modalities
Co-author of an accepted IEEE-EMBS 2025 paper (arXiv:2509.25795) on algorithmic bias in mental health detection
Developing frameworks for ethical and responsible AI deployment

research.summary: Developing interpretable reasoning frameworks and investigating data quality failures in foundation models.
highlights: Investigating synthetic data proliferation and its role in foundation model collapse during recursive training pipelines.
Developed an entailment tree-based framework and benchmark for multi-step logical inference (LOGICAL-COMMONSENSEQA).
Accepted at ACL 2026 (Main Conference) for contributing structured reasoning benchmarks.

research.position: Graduate Researcher – Medical Ethics and NLP
research.summary: Examining the ethical and commonsense reasoning capabilities of LLMs in clinical and biomedical contexts using controlled evaluation pipelines.
highlights: Developed the Medical Ethics Assessment of LLMs project using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline
Analyzed model confidence and rationale structures to assess reliability in moral reasoning tasks
Identified key gaps in ethical reasoning consistency even under knowledge-augmented setups
Contributing to responsible NLP research focused on model interpretability and societal alignment

projects.name: Measuring Model Collapse under Recursive Summarization Training
projects.summary: Investigating the fundamental limits of foundation model training under autophagous (self-consuming) feedback loops. Developing a robust measurement framework to detect early signals of distributional decay and knowledge fidelity loss.
highlights: Designing high-fidelity recursive training pipelines to isolate causal drivers of model collapse
Investigating the theoretical foundations of distributional shift in synthetic data dominant regimes
Developed entropy-based measurement frameworks to detect early signals of systemic output degradation
Analyzing the catalytic role of summarization tasks in accelerating semantic-level information loss

projects.name: Commonsense Reasoning with Logical Entailment Trees
projects.summary: Developed benchmarks and evaluation methods for logical commonsense reasoning to evaluate multi-fact logical capabilities of large language models.
highlights: Created LOGICAL-COMMONSENSEQA, a novel benchmark dataset testing compositional logic
Benchmarked baseline performance with N-Shot and Chain-of-Thought prompting
Designed neuro-symbolic methods combining informal logic with neural approaches
Paper accepted to ACL 2026 (Main Conference)

projects.name: ScoutR: Agentic Football Transfer Intelligence Platform
projects.summary: Designed and shipped an agentic AI transfer intelligence platform that monitors player data across leagues and surfaces candidates aligned to club tactical and financial constraints. Built multi-agent pipelines with Gemini/Claude and Pydantic, and implemented RAG with ChromaDB over StatsBomb event data.
highlights: LangGraph-based multi-agent pipeline with Gemini and Pydantic for complex reasoning
RAG pipeline over StatsBomb event data using ChromaDB for grounded evaluation
Fault-tolerant 3-tier inference layer (Gemini -> Claude -> fallback) for reliability
Real-time streaming agent execution (SSE) for monitoring long-horizon tasks
